>pr description is generated by AI tool

## Motivation

`minimax_decode_topk` has three selection regimes. Two of them already break exact score ties by block id (the lower id wins):

- the small path (`num_blocks <= 128`): `is_greater(...)`, "lower block id wins"
- the ROCm path: a packed `(score, ~id)` total order

The CUDA radix paths (`num_blocks > 128`, i.e. contexts above 16k tokens at block size 128) place the final-round ties in `atomicAdd` order instead. When tied blocks straddle the top-k boundary, the selected set changes from run to run. ROCm indexer CP already depends on a fixed tie order ("requires ... the ROCm radix top-k tie ordering"); the CUDA paths gave no such guarantee.

Exact ties are common for indexers whose keys carry no RoPE: the block score is the max over units, so repeated text produces equal scores. On such a model, serving the same prompts twice from a cold cache with the radix cache on gave 43/45 identical greedy outputs; with this change, 45/45.

## Modifications

- Final radix round: rank the tied candidates by block id (warp ballot + prefix sum) and keep the lowest ids, matching the small and ROCm paths. Applied to both the single-element path and the multi-element (register bucket) path.
- Fast path: when every tie is selected (`equal_count <= topk_remain`), the order does not matter (the output is sorted ascending), so the ties are written with a plain atomic as before and the ranking is skipped.
- Removes the now unused `counter_final`.
- Adds `test_decode_topk_ties_pick_lowest_ids`, which checks the selected set against `(score desc, id asc)` for 300 to 9,000 blocks with heavy ties.

ROCm is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

MiniMax-M3 (bf16, TP8, H200, radix cache on), main vs this PR:

- Greedy outputs on 40 MMLU-Pro prompts plus needle-in-text prompts up to 60k tokens (radix path): 45/45 identical.
- GPQA-Diamond (n=1, max_tokens 32k): 89.4 (main) vs 90.4 (this PR). (range in noise)

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiniMax-M3, TP8, H200, one request at a time, radix cache flushed before each request:

| input tokens | prefill TTFT, main / PR | decode TPOT, main / PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4k | 0.395 / 0.396 s | 13.42 / 13.11 ms |
| 16k | 1.496 / 1.499 s | 13.62 / 13.26 ms |
| 32k | 3.042 / 3.051 s | 13.68 / 13.46 ms |
| 48k | 4.639 / 4.643 s | 13.76 / 13.54 ms |
| 60k | 5.936 / 5.951 s | 13.81 / 13.59 ms |

Kernel microbenchmark (2 heads, 8 to 64 rows, 2k to 8k blocks): within ±0.2 us of main for distinct scores; equal or faster with ties.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No API or behavior change to document.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -118,6 +118,29 @@ def test_decode_topk_adversarial(kind):
         torch.testing.assert_close(a, b, rtol=0, atol=0)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nb", [300, 512, 2000, 3000, 9000])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("levels", [2, 4, 1])
+def test_decode_topk_ties_pick_lowest_ids(nb, levels):
+    """Exactly equal scores are broken by block id (lower id wins), the same rule as
+    the small-row path, so repeated calls select the same blocks: one-element-per-
+    thread rows (nb <= 512) and register-bucket rows (nb > 512)."""
+    torch.manual_seed(nb + levels)
+    block_size = 128
+    H, B, topk = 2, 3, 16
+    score = torch.randint(0, levels, (H, B, nb), device="cuda").float()
+    seq_lens = torch.full((B,), nb * block_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    # reference: order by (score desc, id asc), keep topk, emit ascending
+    want = torch.sort(
+        torch.argsort(-score, dim=-1, stable=True)[..., :topk], dim=-1
+    ).values.to(torch.int32)
+    first = minimax_decode_topk(score, seq_lens, block_size, topk)
+    assert torch.equal(first, want), (first, want)
+    for _ in range(20):
+        assert torch.equal(
+            minimax_decode_topk(score, seq_lens, block_size, topk), first
+        )
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_len", [1, 128, 129, 2048, 2049])
 def test_decode_topk_small_num_blocks(seq_len):
     # num_blocks around / below topk -> naive identity path and boundary.
